To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the students of the skateboarding group significantly outper-formed students of the control-group on the sixth day of a snowboarding school trip.
the students of the skateboarding group performed significantly better in snowboarding than students of the control groups on the last day of the snowboarding school trip.
the experimental group outperformed the control group in terms of snowboarding performance on the sixth day of snowboarding lessons.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how to facilitate learning in snowboarding and other action sports.
the question if and how the knowledge gained from skateboarding can be transferred into snowboarding.
the question of whether or not the transfer of knowledge from skateboarding to the learning of snowboarding is possible.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a preparatory training in skateboarding has a significant facilitation effect on the learning of snowboarding.
skateboarding training can be a valuable addition to snowboarding training.
the transfer of knowledge from skateboarding to learning snowboarding is a reality.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a transfer effect from skateboarding to the learning of snowboarding exists and that the effect is due to the common underlying structure of both sports.
skateboarding lessons are an effective means of preparing students for snowboarding.
a preparatory skateboarding training has a facilitation effect in the learning of snowboarding.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a short, preparatory training on a similar skill set can facilitate learning of a complex motor skill in a different context.
a preparatory skateboard training can be used to improve the learning of snowboarding.
the transfer from skateboarding skills to snowboarding is possible and can be facilitated with preparatory skateboarding training.
